seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [hazard,wall] show mixed outcomes: no_change x2, x x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Floor colour 5 is passable; walls (15 left / 8 right) and any non-5 cell block. A move succeeds only if the 4x4 destination cell is all 5.
Unarmed: A1/A2 move both blocks y-/+4; A3 moves them apart, A4 together (mirrored), each block staying on its own half.
Clicking an inactive marker (9) arms: blocks turn into players (1) and the marker turns active (11). Armed A1-4 move the active marker by 4. Clicking a player disarms; other clicks and A5 do nothing.
HUD: 0-bars along row 0 (right-aligned) and row 63 (left-aligned), width floor(3(a+1)/7). The action count a is continuity-gated; fallback is the smallest a for the shown width.
Refuted hypothesis: the mixed outcome for marker ACTION4 touching [hazard,wall] comes from the destination cell colour, not a global counter. Unconfirmed: what happens when the bar fills, and whether A5 does anything besides ticking the counter.
